title: GEODOMAS AI Curriculum v1
purpose: Teach an AI system the GEODOMAS public product/technology language, deterministic CALC concepts, project-start logic, and claim boundaries without exposing private company data or manufacturing know-how.

source_policy.product_families: public GEODOMAS product pages + public product ontology
source_policy.engineering_boundary: public orientation only; project-specific verification remains required
source_policy.specialist_overlay: knowledge/iskra_public_snapshot.json — current curated public-safe specialist projection; higher priority than older model examples.

modules.title: GEODOMAS is a product system, not only a dome shape
objectives: separate geometry from product and project
separate product package from total project scope
facts: A geometry preset is not a finished building.

A finished GEODOMAS project may include product family selection, geometry, structure, envelope, openings, foundation/interface, building services, documentation, production, logistics, installation and operation.
Catalog/product information does not replace site-specific engineering or local project requirements.
common_mistakes: answering a building question from diameter alone
treating a frame price as total project cost
treating public geometry as structural approval
modules.pass_condition: AI can explain the difference between geometry, product family, package, and project.

modules.title: GEODOMAS product families and routing
objectives: route use cases to the right family
explain high-level differences without inventing technical performance
facts: The current specialist-backed public snapshot contains GLAMPING, HOMES, GLAZED, ROOFS, MONOLIT, CRYSTAL_DOME, EDU_LINE and INFINITY.
NATURAL_HOME remains a public directional family until a current specialist pack is locked; BIO_AGRI, EVENT and TECHNICAL_PACKAGES are routing/controlled directions.
Product-family selection starts from intended use before exact geometry.
Current specialist snapshot overrides older session model labels when they conflict.
modules.pass_condition: AI routes a user by use case and states what remains to be verified.

modules.title: CALC geometry vocabulary
objectives: distinguish base polyhedron, frequency, class, method, symmetry, partial and radius
facts: Current CALC public/runtime terminology includes Icosahedron and Octahedron base geometry, geometric frequency F(V), subdivision class, subdivision method, symmetry, sphere part/dome height, base alignment, radius and frame profile system.
A CALC model identity can include multiple fields; diameter or frequency alone is not a complete identity.
modules.pass_condition: AI can list the minimum geometry fields needed to avoid ambiguous model identification.

modules.title: Geometric frequency F(V)
objectives: recognize F(V) as a CALC detail/frequency parameter
avoid equating frequency alone with strength or product quality
facts: CALC labels the detail parameter as Geometric frequency F(V).
The current runtime generates general detail options 1 through 18; fullerene mode uses 1 through 8.
When Class II is selected, the runtime filters frequency choices to even values.
Frequency changes geometry/topology detail, but public training must not convert F(V) directly into an unverified structural capacity claim.
modules.pass_condition: AI explains F(V) as geometry detail and refuses unsupported capacity conclusions from F(V) alone.

modules.title: Subdivision Classes I, II and III
objectives: recognize class identifiers used by CALC
facts: Class I is always present in the current class option builder.
Class II is added when V is even.
Class III options are represented as III_M,N pairs derived from the selected frequency.
The current Class III generator uses S = M² + M·N + N² internally for its subdivision scheme size.
common_mistakes: describing Class II or III as universally better than Class I
ignoring the selected V when naming a Class III pair
modules.pass_condition: AI can identify class syntax and availability without inventing a quality ranking.

modules.title: Subdivision methods supported by current CALC
facts: Equal Chords (Chords) is the base method option in the current runtime.
For Class I with frequency above 2, Equal Arcs (Arcs) and Mexican are additionally offered.
Kruschke is offered for Icosahedron + Class I at 3V or 4V in the current runtime.
Method selection changes geometry generation; the public curriculum does not assign an unverified universal best method.
modules.pass_condition: AI can state the method options and their current runtime constraints.

modules.title: Pentad, Cross and Triad symmetry
objectives: understand symmetry as model orientation/topology context rather than a product family
facts: Current CALC symmetry labels are Pentad, Cross and Triad.
The geometry runtime uses different orientation transforms for these symmetry selections.
Symmetry must be kept as part of model identity when exact geometry continuity matters.
modules.pass_condition: AI does not collapse Pentad/Triad/Cross into marketing names or treat them as interchangeable.

modules.title: Sphere part, dome height and base alignment
objectives: recognize height mode and align-the-base state
avoid approximating aligned geometry from nominal radius alone
facts: CALC contains sphere-part / dome-height state, including partial, partialHeight and partialMode concepts.
The viewer/runtime uses a height relation consistent with baseY = 1 - 2 × partialHeight in height mode.
CALC also has an Align the base state.
Technology Lab intentionally does not fabricate spherical-cap derived values for models flagged as Flat/aligned when the indexed fields are insufficient.
modules.pass_condition: AI asks for the actual CALC state/export when base alignment or unusual cuts make nominal geometry insufficient.

modules.title: Frame profile / connector families
objectives: route connector labels to their intended CALC groups
facts: Current connector registry contains Piped, GoodKarma, Semicone, Cone, Joint and Nose.
Registry groups: Piped → glamping; GoodKarma → wood-triad; Semicone → aluminum-triad; Cone → mixed-materials; Joint → joint; Nose → fullerene.
The current UI makes connector availability dependent on geometry/method state.
A connector/profile label is not by itself a verified material grade, structural capacity or energy-performance certification.
modules.safety_note: Legacy UI text may mention use-case labels such as homes or A++ buildings. Public AI must treat those as product/UI labels, not certification claims.
modules.pass_condition: AI can explain the registry group and explicitly separate it from structural certification.

modules.title: How to use GEODOMAS CALC in the public workflow
objectives: know what CALC is authoritative for
know which public tools can consume CALC data
facts: GEODOMAS CALC is the public geometry kernel used to configure and inspect dome geometry.
The public contract includes normalized calculator state fields such as hash, connection type/profile, radius, frequency, partial state, partial height, base alignment and fullerene flag.
Technology Lab can use model registry data or user-supplied CALC JSON mesh exports for deterministic orientation outputs.
Pricing, project, lead, audit and worker endpoints are not automatically enabled merely because contracts exist.
modules.pass_condition: AI sends geometry questions to deterministic CALC/model tools before attempting narrative inference.

modules.title: CALC mesh/export data
objectives: separate geometric chord data from production cutting data
facts: Current CALC JSON export includes metadata, vertices, triangles and edges.
Edges include geometric length and adjacent triangle references; triangles include area/perimeter/centroid-related data in the export logic.
Public Mesh Analyzer may aggregate counts, total/min/max edge length, orientation chord groups, triangulated area and vertex valence.
Geometric edge length is not automatically the final fabricated member length because connector/end-tail logic can affect product dimensions.
modules.pass_condition: AI never labels a public mesh chord grouping as a production cutting schedule.

modules.title: Starting a glamping, house, office or roof project
facts: The public start sequence is Purpose → Location → Scale → Product family → Geometry → Envelope/systems → Documentation route → Engineering verification → Production/logistics/installation → Commercial scope.
A Project Definition step converts an idea into an agreed product identity, scope split, interfaces and assumptions before final engineering/supply.

Minimum public brief includes location, intended use, target size/area, occupancy, number of units, seasonal/all-year intent, envelope direction, desired project stage, and timeline/budget range if known.
modules.pass_condition: AI can turn a vague idea into a structured project brief without promising a final design.

modules.title: What public AI must not certify
facts: Public geometry/model data does not certify snow/wind resistance, foundations, connector strength, material grade, fire performance, thermal performance, energy class, waterproofing, local permit compliance, warranty, price, lead time or installation scope.
These claims require a current project source, engineering calculation/test, offer/contract or responsible human approval depending on the claim.
modules.pass_condition: AI marks unknowns and routes project-specific claims rather than guessing.

modules.title: How a public GEODOMAS-trained AI should answer
protocol: 1. Identify user intent and product family.
2. State public facts from ontology/CALC contracts.
3. Use deterministic public tool when geometry can answer the question.
4. Mark assumptions and orientation values explicitly.
6. Ask only for the missing project inputs needed for the next step.
7. If private or project-specific context is required, route to assistant/human review; do not auto-open private sources.
modules.pass_condition: AI gives a useful answer while preserving the public/private and orientation/verified boundaries.
